newsitem.title: FINLAND: Japan to join Finnish nuclear accident rehearsal.
newsitem.headline: Japan to join Finnish nuclear accident rehearsal.

text.p: Japanese experts will join a Finnish-based international nuclear plant accident rehearsal on Thursday, the Finnish Centre for Radiation and Nuclear Safety said on Wednesday.
Hundreds of experts in Europe and beyond will join the practice, to test their responses if an accident were to trigger a leak at the Loviisa nuclear power station on Finland's south coast.

Organiser Hannele Altonen said the Japanese, who had originally not been among the countries due to take part in the exercise, had heard about it after others and decided to join in, bringing to 27 the countries involved outside Finland.
The Japanese government formally asked police on Wednesday to press charges against a state-run firm over a cover-up in its handling of the nation's worst nuclear accident.

Officials of the Japanese Power Reactor and Nuclear Fuel Development Corp (PNC) admitted last week they had lied about procedures followed in dealing with a fire last month at the plant, that triggered an explosion and radiation leak.
The focus of Thursday's practice will be for the authorities to see how to get information out to the public and react.
Any emissions will be imaginary but experts will use real weather and forecasts to try to predict the likely course of radioactive fallout, and the action they would take.
Also built into the test is an assumption that the plant's operators may try to play down the danger.
The exercise is part of a two-year programme by the Nuclear Energy Agency of the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD).
